content: In the R. Ḥurūf Ibn Turka divides practitioners of lettrism into two groups: those concerned with the occult properties of the letters (ahl-i khavāṣṣ), who hold that uttering or contemplating a letter under specific conditions activates its property in the physical or spiritual worlds and who, most prominently al-Būnī, make up the majority; and those concerned with the letters' underlying realities (ahl-i ḥaqāyiq), who seek the meanings and universal sciences the letters contain in terms of the heavenly Book and the isolated quranic letters. He says his purpose is to present a few guiding principles of the latter group.
